theater: 晉南長平郡（今山西晉城東北）

battle.name: 尉文通起義
battle.theater: 晉南長平郡（今山西晉城東北）
battle.brief: 大業六年（610）秋，長平人尉文通聚眾為亂，眾至數萬，攻破長平、沁水一帶縣城；隋煬帝遣相國行軍總管張須陀率郡兵討之。張須陀據道斷糧、設伏誘敵，於長平一戰破之，斬首萬餘級，尉文通僅以身免。卡面埃及長矛未隨軍而至，代表軍陣中數量最多的近身刺擊兵器，隋代由鐵矛與馬槊擔當同一角色。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 大業六年（610）秋，隋朝的河東地面上同時爆發了起義。交戰的一方是隋朝官軍：從中央與州郡徵發的討平軍，主力是河東各郡的郡兵與臨時招募的鄉勇，由相國行軍總管、驃騎將軍張須陀節制，屯兵長平一線，糧食則從洛陽、太原兩個方向輸送。另一方是起義軍：長平本地人尉文通聚眾而起，部眾以本地鄉里民夫、逃籍戶與無業少年為主，人數多而編製散，並與同年起於濟北的王薄、懷州漳水上游的劉向等部互相呼應。值得注意的是，起義方沒有可考的正式編制與旗號，史料只說尉文通「聚眾為亂」；官軍方面也並非全禁軍出動——隋的精銳宿衛與府兵主力這時正準備北征高句麗，能迅速調到長平的，多是郡兵、地方豪強的私兵與臨時募來的勇力。雙方的指揮系統因此都相當簡陋：起義軍靠首領的號召與鄉里的關係網，官軍則靠一名能打的名將在有限時間內集中兵力和就地徵糧。整場衝突從頭到尾是一場低烈度、卻關係到隋朝地方秩序根基的平叛戰。
countriesEn: The rising of Wei Wentong broke out in the autumn of the sixth year of Daye, that is 610 AD, on the Hedong side of the Sui. One side was the Sui field army: a punitive force raised from the centre and from the prefectures and counties, whose core consisted of the local militia of the Hedong commanderies together with village volunteers hired on the spot, placed under the command of Zhang Xutuo, appointed chancellor and chief commander of the expeditionary force, who drew his line along Changping and drew his grain from the directions of Luoyang and Taiyuan. The other side was the insurgents: Wei Wentong, a man of Changping, raised a body of followers made up chiefly of local villagers, men who had fled the register, and landless youths; they were numerous but loosely organised, and they answered one another with the revolt of Wang Bo in Jibei and that of Liu Xiang on the upper reaches of the Zhang river in the same year. It is worth noting that the insurgents had no documented regular establishment and no banner of their own: the sources say only that Wei Wentong 'gathered a crowd and rose in revolt'. Nor was the Sui side sending out the imperial guards: the elite of the Sui, its guard and its militia households, was then preparing for the campaign against Goguryeo, and what could be hurried to Changping was mostly local militia, the private retainers of regional strongmen, and men taken on at short notice. The command structure on both sides was therefore crude. The insurgents relied on the authority of their leader and on the network of village ties; the government relied on a single competent general who had to concentrate troops and gather grain on the spot within a short time. From beginning to end this was a low-intensity affair, and yet it struck at the foundation of Sui order in the localities.
people: 尉文通，長平人，是這場起義唯一留下姓名的首領。史書對他的著墨極少：《隋書》只說他在大業六年聚眾為亂，兵鋒指向長平、沁水一帶，他的出身、族望、年齡都沒有記載，連《資治通鑑》也只重複了《隋書》的骨架。這種空白本身就是資料：他不是像王薄那樣留下檄文、留下旗號的人物，而更像一個在很短時間內被捲入亂局的地方首領，事後仍能脫身。真正改變這場戰爭走向的是隋朝將領張須陀。此人出身行伍，靠平定地方叛亂累功，在隋末的武將群中以善用奇兵、能以少擊眾著稱。他接命之後不急著正面硬撼數萬烏合之眾，而是先據要道、斷糧道、設伏誘敵，再以精騎與銳卒在義軍最脆弱處下手，最終在長平一戰破之。上位者則是隋煬帝楊廣：他在大業初年把主力用於對高句麗的戰備與宮室營造，對河東的亂源卻只能用一位將軍和一點郡兵去堵，顯示朝廷對地方的控制已靠不住。同一時期，郡縣官吏、鄉里豪強與流亡戶之間的張力，使一場饑荒與徵役之下的小規模聚眾，能迅速長成數萬人的隊伍。
peopleEn: Wei Wentong, a native of Changping, is the only leader of this rising whose name has come down to us. The histories say very little about him. The Suishu records only that in the sixth year of Daye he gathered a crowd and rose, his strength directed at Changping and at the neighbourhood of Qinshui; his origin, his standing in his clan and his age are all unrecorded, and the Zizhi Tongjian simply repeats the framework of the Suishu. That silence is itself a piece of evidence: he was not a man who left behind a proclamation or a banner such as those associated with Wang Bo, but rather a local leader swept into the disorder within a very short time, and one who could still get away afterwards. The man who changed the direction of this war was the Sui general Zhang Xutuo. He came up through the ranks and made his name by putting down local revolts, and among the Sui commanders of the last years he was distinguished for using unexpected moves and for beating many with few. On receiving his orders he did not try to meet tens of thousands of the insurgents in open battle, but first held the key roads, cut their supplies and set ambushes to draw them out; then he struck with picked cavalry and picked foot at the weakest point of the rebel line, and finally broke them in a single engagement at Changping. Above both men stood Sui Yangdi, Yang Guang. In the early years of Daye he was committing the main strength to preparations against Goguryeo and to the building of palaces, and against a source of disorder in Hedong he could do no better than send one general and a small number of local troops to plug the hole. That is the measure of how far the court's grip on the localities had slipped. The strain between county officials, village strongmen and men who had fled the register, all of them ground down by conscription and requisition, was such that a small gathering of men could grow within weeks into a body of tens of thousands.
kits: 卡面上這支埃及長矛不會出現在大業六年的長平戰場：它是早王朝時期的埃及兵器，銅或青銅矛頭用繩纏或榫綁在木杆上，用來守城垣，也用來收復失地，是人類最早把「刺」這個動作標準化、把刺擊武器化的一次嘗試。把它放進這場戰爭的裝備表，是因為它佔據的是軍陣中數量最多、門檻最低的那一格——近身刺擊兵器。真正在長平對峙的，是中國的矛與槊：隋代郡兵與鄉勇手中的長矛，鐵或鋼的矛頭安在長木杆上，既是步卒結陣時的骨幹，也是農民軍把鋤、叉、削尖的竹木改造過來的現成器械；騎兵所用的馬槊在隋唐之際已經是標準裝備，同樣是長杆前端加刃，捅、架、蕩三種動作並用。與矛並列的是刀：隋庫中的橫刀、陌刀用於劈砍與馬上搏鬥；弓弩負責遠程，弩機在魏晉南北朝已經成熟，是官軍在遠距離上壓制人數優勢的依仗；護具方面有明光甲與馬鎧，隋的騎兵正從輕騎向具裝過渡，但整體裝備仍以皮革與少量金屬為主。攻城與守城的器物包括巢車、雲梯、撞車、投石車與穴地掘進的地道，城上則佈置拒馬與覆幢。運輸靠牛車，人力輔以沁水、丹水的小船；糧食是這場戰爭真正的瓶頸。埃及那支矛在此只作為技術譜系的代表：從早王朝的銅矛，到隋代的鐵矛，中間是同一條線的延伸。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card would not have been present on the field at Changping in the sixth year of Daye. It is an Egyptian weapon of the Old Kingdom: a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft with cord or a tenon, used to defend city walls and used to recover lost ground, and it is one of the earliest attempts to standardise the act of thrusting and to turn the thrusting arm into a weapon in its own right. It belongs in the equipment table of this war because it occupies the largest and least demanding slot in any order of battle, the close-combat thrusting arm. What actually faced each other at Changping was the Chinese spear and the shao. The long spears carried by the Sui militia and by the village volunteers had iron or steel heads fixed to long wooden shafts; they were the backbone of the foot soldier's order of battle, and they were also what the peasant bands made of hoes, forks and sharpened bamboo and wood. The horse shao, standard equipment for cavalry at the turn of Sui and Tang, was the same idea: a blade at the end of a long shaft, used to thrust, to parry and to sweep. Alongside the spear stood the sabre. The hengdao and the modao kept in the Sui treasuries were for cutting and for fighting on horseback, while the bow and the crossbow supplied the long range, the trigger mechanism of the crossbow having been mature since the Wei, Jin and Northern and Southern dynasties, and it was on the crossbow that the government troops relied to check the numerical advantage of the crowd at long distance. For protection there were the bright armour of the Ming Guang type and the caparison of the horse; Sui cavalry was in transition from light horse to fully armoured horse, but the equipment as a whole still ran largely on leather with only a little metal. The siege and defence works included the nest-cart, the scaling ladder, the battering ram, the stone-thrower and the digging of tunnels under the walls, while the defenders set up caltrops and mantlets on the walls. Transport was by ox cart, assisted by small boats on the Qin and the Dan rivers, and grain was the real bottleneck of this war. The Egyptian spear stands here only as the representative of a line of technique: from the copper spear of the Old Kingdom to the iron spear of the Sui, with the same thread running between them.
tactics: 起義軍的戰法是典型的流民式野戰：起事之後先攻縣城、破府庫、取糧食，再退回鄉里與山地，避開官軍主力，據險待變，靠人數與地理拖延。尉文通據長平，太行山南麓的山口與沁水、丹水兩條河谷是他們轉移的孔道，晉城盆地既是糧食來源，也是義軍補充人手的所在。官軍這邊，張須陀用的是隋軍平叛的標準手段加上自己的經驗：先不急著爭地盤，而是以少量精兵守住長平與壺關之間的通道，切斷義軍與外界、與王薄部的聯繫；然後誘敵離開村落，把烏合之眾拉進自己選定的戰場，一次紮營，一次夜襲，一次決戰，一次追擊。史書記他破尉文通時「斬首萬餘級」，可知戰果主要來自一次會戰而不是圍城；義軍潰散之後，官軍騎兵在山道與河谷中收拾散卒，堵住復合之路。整場戰事從秋末打到冬初，時間不長，因為雙方都不具備長期圍城與消耗的條件：義軍的糧食靠搶，官軍的糧食靠運，運不過來的時候，義軍就等於失敗。
tacticsEn: The way the insurgents fought was the typical fluid warfare of dispossessed peasants. After raising the revolt they struck first at the county towns, broke open the granaries and the treasuries, took grain, and then withdrew back into the villages and the hills, avoiding the main body of the government troops, holding difficult ground and waiting for the situation to turn, prolonging the contest by numbers and by geography. Wei Wentong's base was Changping, and the passes of the southern slope of the Taihang together with the valleys of the Qin and the Dan rivers were the corridors through which his bands moved; the Jincheng basin was both a source of grain and the place where the insurgents drew fresh hands. On the government side Zhang Xutuo used the standard methods of a Sui suppression campaign together with his own experience. He did not rush to seize ground; with a small picked force he held the corridor between Changping and Hanguan, cutting the insurgents off both from the outside world and from Wang Bo's men. Then he drew them out of their villages, led the motley crowd onto ground of his own choosing, and struck once in camp, once by night attack, once in the battle and once in the pursuit. The sources record that in breaking Wei Wentong he cut off more than ten thousand heads, which shows that the result came from a single pitched engagement rather than from a siege; when the insurgents broke, government cavalry swept up the stragglers along the mountain tracks and river valleys and closed the road by which the bands might re-form. The whole affair ran from the late autumn into the beginning of winter and was not long, because neither side could afford a long siege or a war of attrition: the insurgents got their grain by plunder, the government got its grain by transport, and when transport failed the insurgents had already lost.
data: 可核對的數字不多，但有幾個是硬的。第一，時點：起義繫於大業六年，即公元610年，編年史書多把平亂記在這一年的秋冬之交，一般落在十月前後，具體日干支不見於他書。第二，規模：《隋書》與《資治通鑑》都說尉文通聚眾為亂，眾至數萬；同樣在這一年，起義並非孤例，王薄起兵於濟北與長平一帶，劉向起兵於懷州漳水上游，隋廷同時用兵，兵分則力薄，這是當時的局面寫照。第三，戰果：張須陀破尉文通，斬首萬餘級，尉文通本人趁夜遁走，僅以身免。第四，隋朝這時可倚賴的兵與糧：《隋書·地理志》所載隋代州縣總數在州百數十、縣千一百上下，各郡能自募的郡兵人數有限，而大業六年正在備戰第一次征高句麗，精銳與糧秣大量集中在東北的涿郡、萊州一線，河東的防線因此空虛。第五，地理數字：長平在太行山南麓，東連壺關以通太原，南出河內以達洛陽方向，由長平至京師的道路約七百餘里，唐宋之制一里約合今半公里，一日急行軍可走百餘里。凡此數字，除「萬餘級」一條外皆為推算，只能用來框定量級，不能當作精確傷亡。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, but a few of them are hard. First, the date: the rising is tied to the sixth year of Daye, 610 AD, and the annalistic histories place the suppression in the late autumn and early winter of that year, generally around the tenth month; the exact day and the cyclical day stem are not given elsewhere. Second, the scale: both the Suishu and the Zizhi Tongjian say that Wei Wentong gathered a crowd and rose, the number running to tens of thousands. The rising was no isolated affair in that year, for Wang Bo was in arms in Jibei and around Changping and Liu Xiang was in arms on the upper Zhang in the prefecture of Huai, and the Sui court was fighting on several fronts at once with its strength thus divided, and that is the picture of the time. Third, the result: Zhang Xutuo broke Wei Wentong and cut off more than ten thousand heads, while Wei Wentong himself escaped by night and got away with nothing but his life. Fourth, the men and grain the Sui could count on: the Geography Treatise of the Suishu gives the totals of the Sui as a little over a hundred and ten prefectures and some eleven hundred counties, so the militia any one commandery could raise by recruitment was limited, and in the sixth year of Daye preparations for the first campaign against Goguryeo were drawing the elite and the grain towards the north-east, to the line of Zhuojun and Laizhou, which left Hedong thinly held. Fifth, geography: Changping lay on the southern slope of the Taihang, linked on the east to Hanguan on the road to Taiyuan and on the south to Hnei on the way towards Luoyang, and the road from Changping to the capital ran to something over seven hundred li, a Tang or Song li being about half a kilometre, so that a forced march covered a little over a hundred li a day. Except for the figure of 'more than ten thousand heads', all of these are estimates; they can fix the order of magnitude and nothing more, and they must not be read as exact losses.
cause: 要打起來，理由可以分成四層。第一層是國家的財政與徭役：大業初年隋朝連續經營東征高句麗的準備與宮室營造，兵役、徭役、租調一齊加到州縣頭上，史臣評隋文帝末政用過「役使百端，天下始弊」一語，正是指這一段的積累。第二層是徵役的具體樣子：大業六年前後，天下適齒男子一批一批被調往北方以及江都方向的工地與軍鎮，山西、河北一帶大量丁口脫戶與逃籍，留在鄉里的丁壯要供糧、要輸稅、還要隨官軍徵發，一旦歉收或遇上官府苛索，隨時會有人號召抗拒。第三層是地方治理的薄弱：隋朝在河東的州縣官幾年一換，郡兵久不操練，縣城的城守與糧秣儲備都不堪倚靠，尉文通起事之後能連下長平、沁水一帶的縣，說明地方機構在數日之間就失去了抵抗能力。第四層是民間的信仰與組織：彌勒信仰在民間流傳已久，隋朝把它視為悖亂的苗頭而屢加禁絕，民間的結社與彌勒式的口號為起事提供了現成的語言；大業七年冀州趙孝義聚眾起事的記載，說明大業六年之後南北已各有火種。至於尉文通本人為什麼起事，史料沒有留下任何解釋，只留下他聚眾這個事實本身。
causeEn: There are four layers to the reasons for the fighting. The first is the finances and the labour service of the state. In the early years of Daye the Sui was carrying on preparations for repeated campaigns against Goguryeo and the building of palaces, and the levies, the corvees and the taxes were all loaded onto the prefectures and counties at once; the judgement of the historian on the closing years of Wendi's reign, that 'the people were put to every service and the realm began to wear out', is aimed precisely at this accumulation. The second is what the conscription actually looked like. Around the sixth year of Daye the men of military age were taken away to the north and to the works and the garrisons in the direction of Jiangdu in ever greater numbers, and in Shanxi and in Hebei a large part of the registered households slipped away; those who stayed had to supply grain, to pay tax and to answer the levy, and once a harvest failed or the officials grew exacting, there was always someone ready to call for refusal. The third is the thinness of local government. The Sui rotated its officials in Hedong every few years, the county militia had long gone untrained, and neither the defence of the county walls nor the store of grain could be relied upon; the fact that Wei Wentong could take one county after another in the districts of Changping and Qinshui shows that the local institutions lost the capacity to resist within a matter of days. The fourth is the faith and organisation of the villages. The cult of Maitreya had long circulated among the people, and the Sui regarded it as the seed of rebellion and forbade it repeatedly, but the associations of the villages and the Maitreyan formulas gave any rising a ready language; the record of Zhao Xiaoyi gathering a band in Jizhou in the seventh year of Daye shows that after the sixth year there was a fire lit in the north as well as in the south. As for Wei Wentong himself, the sources offer no explanation whatever; they give only the fact that he gathered a crowd.
impact: 尉文通起義的直接戰果只有一場短促的平叛，但它在隋朝歷史上的位置並不低。第一，它是大業六年那一年標誌性事件的先聲：同一年裡，北方有王薄與尉文通，南方有劉向與江淮的彌勒信仰餘波，隋朝的財政、兵制與地方控制同時亮起紅燈，隋末大亂的時間表從這一年正式起算。第二，它暴露了隋朝真正的問題不是沒有兵，而是兵不該在何處。張須陀靠郡兵與臨時募來的勇力打贏了這場仗，說明中央的宿衛與府兵主力被北征牽制，地方上只剩下地方人的地方兵；一旦地方兵連續被拉去平叛，地方社會的武裝化就無法逆轉。第三，它把張須陀推上了歷史前台，而張須陀的結局恰好說明隋朝的沒落：此後他在幽州平定高位祖，在河北與竇建德部交戰，大業九年陣歿，隋廷失去了當時最能打的方面將領，亂局此後再也壓不下去。第四，在考古與地理上，長平郡一帶自戰國到隋唐一直是兵家必爭之地，今山西晉城、高平一帶的古城遺址與兵器銘文提供的是長期的地緣背景，而不是610年這一場戰鬥的直接證據；關於這場起義的全部文字依據，仍然只有《隋書》與《資治通鑑》那幾行。
impactEn: The direct result of the rising of Wei Wentong was a single short suppression, but its place in Sui history is not small. First, it is the opening note of what the sixth year of Daye stands for. In that same year the north had Wang Bo and Wei Wentong, the south had Liu Xiang and the after-current of Maitreyan belief in the Jiang and the Huai, and the finances, the military system and the local control of the Sui all showed red at once; the timetable of the great disorder of the late Sui dates its start from that year. Second, it exposed the real problem, which was not that the Sui had no soldiers but where those soldiers were not. Zhang Xutuo won with the militia of the commanderies and with men taken on at short notice, which shows that the central guard and the militia households were tied down by the northern campaign and that what was left to the localities was the locals' own troops; once local troops were pulled into one suppression after another, the arming of the localities could not be reversed. Third, it thrust Zhang Xutuo onto the stage of history, and his end illustrates the decline of the Sui exactly. He afterwards put down Gao Weizu in Youzhou, fought Dou Jiande's men in Hebei, and fell in the field in the ninth year of Daye; the court had lost the most capable of its field commanders, and the disorder could never be pressed down again after that. Fourth, in archaeology and geography, the Changping district had been a place armies fought over from the Warring States through Sui and Tang, and the ancient city sites and the inscribed weapons of the Jincheng and Gaoping area give a long geographical background rather than direct evidence for the fighting of 610; the entire written basis for this rising remains the few lines in the Suishu and the Zizhi Tongjian.
result: 大業六年秋冬，尉文通的隊伍在長平被張須陀擊潰：《隋書》與《資治通鑑》都記官軍斬首萬餘級，義軍主力當場瓦解，部眾或死於戰陣，或散歸田里，一部分併入其他義軍。尉文通本人卻趁夜逃出，僅以身免，此後的史料再沒有交代他的下落——這是本場戰爭最耐人尋味的一筆：平掉的是兵，不是亂源。對隋廷而言，此役是一次及時的止血：長平一線的通道重新打開，河東的郡縣得以恢復收稅與徵兵，張須陀因此名聲大振，隋煬帝得以把注意力轉回遼東的戰事。但代價同樣清楚：每一場平叛都要臨時徵發糧秣與鄉勇，都要從別處抽調兵將，而別處的兵將正在遼東與江南作戰。三年之後大業九年的江都之變、七年之後的瓦崗與關中並起，說明這次止血只延遲了崩潰，沒有改變方向。尉文通起義留下的，是隋朝末期地方秩序失效的第一份公開記錄，也是一份關於「以兵平亂」的警告。
resultEn: In the late autumn and early winter of the sixth year of Daye, Wei Wentong's force was broken at Changping by Zhang Xutuo. Both the Suishu and the Zizhi Tongjian record that the government troops cut off more than ten thousand heads; the main body of the insurgents collapsed on the spot, and the men were either killed in the battle or scattered back to their fields, some of them joining other rebel bands. Wei Wentong himself, however, escaped in the night and got away with nothing but his life, and no later source says what became of him. That is the most suggestive stroke in the whole affair: what was put down was an army, not the source of the disorder. For the court the affair was a timely stoppage of the bleeding. The corridor along Changping was opened again, the commanderies of Hedong could resume collecting tax and levying men, Zhang Xutuo became famous, and Sui Yangdi was able to turn his attention back to the war in the north-east. But the price was just as clear. Every suppression demanded grain and village volunteers gathered at short notice, and every one of them pulled troops and generals away from somewhere else, and those somewheres were fighting in Liaodong and in the south of the river. Three years later the mutiny at Jiangdu in the ninth year of Daye, and seven years later the rising at Wagang and in Guanzhong, show that this stopping of the bleeding only postponed the collapse and changed nothing about its direction. The rising of Wei Wentong left behind the first public record of the failure of local order in the late Sui, and with it a warning about putting down disorder with soldiers.
